advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reject/validate identity key lines (single-line, no control chars, well-formed authorized-keys) before rendering them into the SSHSIG allowed_signers trust root in allowed_signers_from_keys
evidence: authorship.py: `return "\n".join(f"{principal} {key_line.strip()}" for key_line in keys if key_line and key_line.strip())` — .strip() only trims leading/trailing whitespace, leaving interior '\n' intact
The rendered blob is the trust root written to the allowed_signers file and passed to `ssh-keygen -Y verify -f signers_path` (src/rebar/attest/sshsig.py:138-155)

`keys` are stored verbatim with no format/newline/control-char validation at creation: src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:184-188 copies `identity['keys']` directly, and src/rebar/_commands/identity.py:250-252 appends each `--key` raw value without validation

An embedded newline in a key line lets an attacker who controls an identity's `keys` inject additional allowed_signers directives (e.g. `cert-authority`, wildcard principals, options) into that identity's trust root
advisory.finding: allowed_signers_from_keys interpolates identity key lines into the SSHSIG trust-root file with only .strip() (which does not remove interior newlines), so a key value containing an embedded newline injects extra allowed_signers lines/options consumed by ssh-keygen — an allowed_signers injection that can broaden the identity's trust root.
scenarios: An identity's `keys` list contains a value with an interior newline (via library create_identity(keys=[...]) or an imported/edited identity ticket), injecting an extra trust-root line/option that ssh-keygen then honors during verify
advisory.suggested_fix: Validate each key_line before use: skip or reject any entry containing control characters or interior newlines (reuse sshsig._has_control_chars), and require a single well-formed `"<keytype> <base64>"` token pair — not merely .strip().

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test for `allowed_signers_from_keys` with a blank/whitespace entry (skipped) and multiple keys (one line each, newline-joined).
evidence: src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:67-69: `return "\n".join(f"{principal} {key_line.strip()}" for key_line in keys if key_line and key_line.strip())`
ABSENCE: no test passes a `keys` list containing a blank/whitespace entry or more than one key to create_identity/resolve_trust_root, so the filter and multi-line join branches are uncovered.
advisory.finding: The documented blank/whitespace-skipping and multi-key newline-join behavior of `allowed_signers_from_keys` is never exercised: every test (roundtrip, cross-identity, trust-root) creates identities with exactly one non-blank key, so the `if key_line and key_line.strip()` filter and the multi-element `"\n".join(...)` are only ever hit with a single element. A regression that failed to skip a blank/whitespace key entry (emitting a malformed `<principal> ` allowed_signers line) or mis-joined multiple keys would pass the entire suite.
scenarios: An identity ticket with an empty-string or whitespace key entry alongside a real key
An identity with two recorded public keys (key rotation)
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a direct unit test: `assert authorship.allowed_signers_from_keys(['', '  ', 'ssh-ed25519 AAAA', 'ssh-ed25519 BBBB'], principal='id-1') == 'id-1 ssh-ed25519 AAAA\nid-1 ssh-ed25519 BBBB'`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a roundtrip test where an identity records two keys and the payload is signed with the second key, asserting verified is True.
evidence: Roundtrip signs and verifies with a single-key identity: tests/unit/test_identity_bde5.py:70-78
resolve_trust_root binds ALL `keys` to the principal: src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:92-95
ABSENCE: no test creates an identity with >1 key and signs with a non-first key.
advisory.finding: No test verifies that an author with MULTIPLE in-band keys can verify a payload signed with any one of them (e.g. the second/rotated key). The in-band-keys trust model implies any recorded key of the identity is a valid signer, but the roundtrip only signs with a single-key identity's sole key.
scenarios: Key rotation: an identity records two keys and an older/newer key signs the payload
